relatedSnapshot.title: Adding leads to an existing campaign wipes the campaign's existing leads while still consuming credits
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Name 4 signal (daily triage 2026-07-29)

Name 4 cluster *Campaign leads vanish after new upload, credits consumed* — severity high, confidence 0.88, **2 customers this week**.

* **Name 2 (Company One)**: 5,347 existing leads in a campaign disappeared when she added more leads to it.
* **Name 3**: hit the same data-loss pattern today.

In both cases the leads are gone and the credits were still charged, so the customer pays twice to rebuild the list.

Name 4 topic: <url>

## Why this is a new issue

Duplicate search found no open canonical for "adding leads wipes the existing lead set":

* ENG-10981 "Scraped leads disappear after processing — credits consumed, campaign stays empty" — Done (2026-06-29); different trigger (initial scrape, not a second upload into a populated campaign)
* ENG-8186 "Cold Email Agent lead count resets after import" — Done (2026-05-03)
* ENG-7942 "Campaign upload loses leads and skips to step 4" — Done
* ENG-4551 "Missing ~760 leads after CSV import" — Done
* ENG-7247 / ENG-7186 — deletion/duplicate-skip behaviour, not data loss on add

Distinct from the stuck-processing cluster on ENG-10762: here the leads were present and are afterwards gone.

## Suggested starting points

* The add-leads path into an existing campaign: whether the import replaces rather than appends the campaign lead set
* Credit deduction on the second import happening before/independently of the lead write, so credits are consumed even when the resulting lead set shrinks

## Triage metadata

* Name 5 key: `modem_daily_triage:v1/<uuid>/2026-07-29`
* Window: 2026-07-28 13:02 UTC → 2026-07-29 13:02 UTC
* Recurrence: recurring, 2 customers this week

relatedSnapshot.title: Customer report: purchased campaign leads hard-deleted by automatic completed-campaign cleanup, campaign shows 0 leads while History still reports the uploads
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Source

Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>
Contact: Name 2, Company One Workspace. The Intercom source URL points directly at the campaign in view: "Management Consulting | Name 6 | May 2026".

## Conversation context (bounded)

The customer reports that 5,000 leads purchased for that campaign went missing, that the total is now 7,802, and that it has been over a month without resolution. She says the Leads tab History view shows uploads while the campaign table shows 0 leads, and that she did not delete them: "when I purchased more leads the first time there was an issue the first 5000 disappeared, I purchased 1500 more and now they are also gone." She asks whether a record of the purchased leads exists, then asked for a human agent. Fin AI replied with the History view and deletion-recovery guidance; no human has answered.

## Claim

Leads purchased for a cold email campaign are hard-deleted from that campaign by the platform's automatic completed-campaign lead removal, which a later lead purchase triggers when the workspace is short on provider lead space, so the campaign ends up with 0 leads while its Leads tab History still reports every purchase as uploaded.

## Evidence

* Production: the campaign holds 0 lead rows (including soft-deleted); its Leads tab History holds 18 lead sources totalling 7,969 leads recorded as uploaded.
* Production activity log: "Deleted all 5686 leads from campaign" at 2026-07-27T17:03:04Z and "Deleted all 2630 leads from campaign" at 2026-10-02T18:19:05Z, both on this campaign.
* Name 7: Inngest run 01M3YXDZ55D5P0723AXMDM7EW1 (ai-clients.campaigns.process-delete-all-leads, COMPLETED 2026-10-02T18:19:06Z) returned deletedFromDb 2630, providerDeletedCount 2531; its step trace contains classify-final-capacity-plan, a step that only runs on the automatic-completed-campaign-cleanup branch. The deletion followed a lead purchase for a different campaign by 23 seconds.
* Code: process-lead-generator.ts sends PROCESS_LEAD_REMOVAL when provider lead space is low; process-lead-removal.ts fans out campaign-delete-all-leads with deletionSource automatic_completed_campaign_cleanup for every Completed campaign; process-campaign-delete-all-leads.ts deletes at the provider then calls deleteAllLeadsByCampaign (hard delete, all rows, no recency guard).
* Blast radius (queried 2026-10-05): 727 "Deleted all N leads from campaign" activity rows across 245 organizations in the last 30 days, 221 of them within 15 minutes after a lead purchase for the same organization; 3,032 campaigns currently in Completed status still holding live leads across 1,416 organizations.
* Related open work: ENG-12122 (this same customer and campaign, 5,347 leads reported lost on 2026-07-29, Urgent, Blocked) and ENG-11215 (sibling automatic cleanup hard-deleting campaign lead lists, Backlog).

relatedSnapshot.title: Add on-demand sync of missing campaign leads by email filter
relatedSnapshot.description:
# Add on-demand sync of missing campaign leads by email filter

## Problem Statement

When searching for campaign leads by email in the database, if those leads don't exist locally but do exist on the provider platform (e.g., Company Two.ai), there's no automatic mechanism to sync them. This requires manual intervention and delays workflows.

## Solution Overview

This PR adds on-demand syncing capability to `OutreachRepository.findCampaignLeadsByEmails`:

* When `shouldSyncIfNotFound` option is enabled and no leads are found locally
* The system queries the provider API with email filter
* Bulk imports the found leads using `processBulkLeads`
* Retries the lookup to return the newly synced data

## Technical Changes

1. **Backend (Outreach)**:
   * Enhanced `OutreachRepository.findCampaignLeadsByEmails` with optional `shouldSyncIfNotFound` parameter
   * Fetches provider campaign via `OutreachService` and calls `providerClient.listLeads(campaignId, p, email)` to find leads by email
   * Bulk imports found leads via `processBulkLeads` and retries lookup
2. **Reusable Bulk Processing**:
   * Exported `processBulkLeads` from `lib/inngest/functions/outreach/campaign-leads-import.ts` for external use
3. **Provider Interface**:
   * Extended `OutreachProvider.listLeads` to accept optional `email` filter parameter

## Impact

* Reduces manual intervention for missing lead data
* Improves data completeness automatically
* Enables more seamless lead lookup workflows

## Related PR

* PR #1130: <url:github.com>

relatedSnapshot.title: Master: Help reps respond quickly with reliable notifications
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a client replies or calls, the responsible rep should notice quickly and open the right conversation. Make text alerts work first, then improve call reliability, connected-mailbox replies and delivery failures. Add more advanced browser delivery and personal controls afterwards.

## Problem

A client asked how to know when emails and texts arrive so they can respond immediately. Incoming text alerts are currently unwired, connected mailboxes do not yet have complete automatic reply ingestion, and calling readiness can look successful when this browser is not ready. A popup is only useful if it reaches the right person and leaves a dependable place to find the work later.

## What's included

* Immediate text alerts, reliable live call popups, email reply alerts and failed-text recovery notifications.
* A personal notification entry available throughout the authenticated app, with workspace context and a persistent unread indicator.
* Top-right pop-ups, desktop notifications and sounds, a rebuilt drawer, workspace alerts in the top bar and personal notification settings with quiet hours; closed-tab browser push after that.
* Routing by actual responsibility and current access. Closers receive their work; managers receive explicitly assigned exceptions; operators receive service issues they can fix.
* Integration with the existing Conversations, missed-call, mailbox-sync and workspace-settings work below.
* A controlled AI Acquisition LT pilot with delivery, duplicate and permission evidence before wider rollout.

## Execution order

Owner: Elis. Use the lowest-numbered eligible ticket first. Tickets grouped as parallel may start together when there is capacity, but keep the priority order. Waves show the earliest unlock, not a barrier: start a later-wave ticket as soon as its own blockers are done. Each delivery ticket targets one PR of roughly 2,000 lines or less. The approved exception is ENG-13772, which coordinates eight nested deliveries under its own execution order and retains its complete acceptance and downstream blockers.

**Design**

Current design (5 Oct 2026): Notifications kit, clickable. Each child has its own screenshots and deep links; the playground's bottom half shows every notification card grouped by ticket. The prototype is private until James shares it; the screenshots here are the same frames.

| View | Link |
| -- | -- |
| Playground (Simulate bar, every control, card catalogue) | Open |
| Drawer, Inbox | Open |
| Drawer with a text open (inline reply) | Open |
| Drawer with an AI SDR escalation open | Open |
| Drawer with the overdue digest open | Open |
| Drawer, Alerts filter | Open |
| Drawer, Tasks filter | Open |
| Snoozed / Done tabs | Snoozed / Done |
| Empty / Loading / Error | Empty / Loading / Error |
| Dismissed alert (Unresolved in drawer) | Open |
| Pop-up stack (hover to fan) | Open |
| Text burst | Open |
| Incoming call (Enter answers, Name 21 declines) | Open |
| Away: desktop banners, tab count | Open |
| Away: caller hung up | Open |
| Settings › Notifications | Open |
| Settings, desktop permission blocked | Open |
| Settings, microphone blocked | Open |
| Settings, phone line offline | Open |
| Settings, closed-tab notifications on | Open |
| Conversations, text not delivered + exact message highlighted | Open |
| Card catalogue for one ticket | Add `.cards-eng-<id>` to the playground link, e.g. ENG-13780 |

Card catalogue per child: ENG-13431, ENG-13433, ENG-13775, ENG-13777, ENG-13779, ENG-13780, ENG-13812, ENG-13817, ENG-13819, ENG-13821.

**Workspace alerts in the top bar (worst first, +N, click to list all)**

 <image> 

**Drawer, Inbox: floating card under the bell (light)**

 <image> 

**Drawer, Inbox (dark)**

 <image> 

**Pop-up stack under the bell (light)**

 <image> 

**Incoming call ringing (light)**

 <image> 

**Settings › Notifications (light)**

 <image> 

Superseded, do not build from: the 13 Sep prototype (link) and the design packs attached before 5 Oct.

### Wave 1: can start now

Parallel: 1, 2 and 3 touch different code and can run together.

1. Quick notification fixes: duplicate overdue tasks, placeholder text and the invitation-cancelled email: small fixes, no design needed.
2. Notify reps when a client texts back, and keep failed texts visible: the client ask. Works on today's drawer first.
3. Own the notification store and live updates: nothing visible; everything in Wave 2 onwards is built on it.

### Wave 2: starts when the notification store (3) is done

Parallel: 4 and 5 are the two big UI pieces and can run together. 6, 7, 8 and 9 each add notification types in separate areas and can run alongside 4 and 5 and each other.

4. Pop-ups, incoming calls, desktop notifications and sounds: blocked by 3.
5. Rebuild the notification drawer: blocked by 3.
6. Notify reps about replies and the AI SDR, and let them act from the card: blocked by 3.
7. Tell workspaces when campaigns, sending or integrations need attention: blocked by 3.
8. Notify people about missed calls, bookings, phone line problems and Zoom: blocked by 3.
9. Notify reps about tasks due now, tasks assigned to them and changes to their deals: blocked by 3 and 1.

### Wave 3: starts as individual Wave 2 tickets finish

Parallel: 10, 11 and 12.

10. Show workspace alerts in the top bar: blocked by 5.
11. Personal notification settings and closed-tab notifications: blocked by 4.
12. Notify reps when connected-mailbox replies arrive: blocked by 2 and 3. Also can't go live until Ebubeker's mailbox sync ships: ENG-12668, ENG-2061 (Gmail), ENG-12972 (Microsoft).

Cross-wave overlap:

* 10 may start when 5 finishes, while 4 and 6 to 9 are still underway.
* 11 may start when 4 finishes, while 5 and 6 to 9 are still underway.
* 12 may start once 2 and 3 are done, alongside anything in Wave 2.

### Wave 4: last

13. Move billing warnings onto alerts and retire Name 22: blocked by 5, 10 and billing ENG-13746, ENG-13360, ENG-13745, ENG-11454. Each billing warning can switch over as soon as its billing ticket ships; Name 22 is removed at the end.

### Backlog: ticketed, parked until James moves them to To do

14. Notify people about team changes, <mention> and account security: blocked by 3.
15. Notify people about meeting recordings, AI tools, websites and domains: blocked by 3.
16. Show failed texts in the new notification feed and let reps retry safely: blocked by 3 and 5, and by Show inbound text alerts in the new notification feed. Moved out of ENG-13431 on 6 Oct 2026; follow-up, not MVP.

**Billing is not blocked by any of this.** ENG-13746, ENG-13360, ENG-13745 and ENG-11454 (Anthony) ship with email and today's drawer first. ENG-13777 is the only place the two meet.

**Merged or closed:** 14 Sep, 27 tickets were consolidated into these 15 and the old owners archived. ENG-11552 is a duplicate of ENG-13776. A Meta ad failing to publish was deliberately left out.

## Role and routing defaults

| Recipient | Default attention |
| -- | -- |
| Closer or SDR | Replies for their assigned receiving line, bound mailbox or explicitly owned conversation; live calls only for their eligible line |
| Covering rep | Work explicitly assigned through coverage; unresolved items transfer when responsibility changes |
| Manager | Unassigned or conflicting work and agreed escalation exceptions; no sound for every rep's message |
| Workspace operator | Routing, mailbox, line or integration problems they are authorized to fix |
| Read-only member | Authorized content and personal notification controls; no new sending, reassignment or shared-resolution rights |

AI Acquisition LT's audit found empty closer/SDR teams and sparse contact ownership. Do not broadcast to a role or use contact owner alone. Use the receiving-line assignee for the first text release and identify an authorized fallback before the pilot. This routing decision is separate from assigning engineering tickets.

## Existing work this master coordinates

| Outcome | Canonical work | Treatment |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Current inbound call engine and first-use audio setup | ENG-12193, ENG-12191 | Already Done. Pop-ups, incoming calls, desktop notifications and sounds addresses audited remaining gaps, not a rebuild. |
| Missed calls and voicemail follow-up | ENG-12494, with ENG-12334 for protected recordings | Preserve the existing ticket. Proposed notification integration addendum is included in this draft. |
| Conversations and personal CRM unread / Needs reply | ENG-12504, ENG-12498 | Keep existing ownership and parents. Alert the responsible rep when a client texts back uses the existing contact route and personal notification state. |
| Connected-mailbox binding and automatic sync | ENG-12668, ENG-2061, ENG-12972 | Provider state stays here; Notify reps when connected-mailbox replies arrive consumes newly persisted replies. |
| Email replies inside Conversations | ENG-13342 | Keep canonical screen/composer work here. |
| Workspace email recipients for workflow, AI SDR and Cold Email Agent notifications | ENG-8419 | Preserve its admin/owner settings, empty-selection disables email, Resend and existing Slack contract. |
| AI SDR alerts and its own unread badge | ENG-6466, ENG-4202 | Related work; Notify reps when connected-mailbox replies arrive is connected Gmail/Microsoft mail, not another AI SDR notification implementation. |
| Customer reports about clearing/mismatched notifications | ENG-13184, ENG-12096 | Retain as evidence and verify separately before resolving them. |
| New booking, confirmation, joining soon, payment follow-up, no-show | ENG-11548, ENG-11549, ENG-11550, ENG-11551, ENG-11555 | Existing automations own when these events happen. Reuse notification delivery when each is ready. |

## Later expansion

The current Execution order above governs the active campaign, AI and billing scope. Work outside those 15 tickets remains later expansion: manager response-time escalation and coverage automation; optional Slack reply delivery in ENG-12095; richer notification filters and reporting.

These remain explicit follow-on scope in this master, not acceptance criteria secretly added to Alert the responsible rep when a client texts back. Before starting an uncovered extension, choose its next complete user journey and draft it for review. Native mobile push and answering calls with the browser closed need a separate product/delivery decision.

## Done when

* A new text reaches only the responsible authorized rep, shows promptly, survives refresh and opens the correct conversation.
* Calls show and stop correctly across routes and tabs; readiness problems are visible and recoverable.
* New Gmail and Microsoft replies are detected without opening CRM and reach the correct rep; imports and duplicates stay quiet.
* Failed texts remain visible after navigation and never encourage a duplicate send.
* Closed-tab notification behavior and unsupported states are tested and explained accurately.
* Read/unread, dismiss, conversation Needs reply and shared resolution have separate meanings; another rep's activity cannot erase personal unread.
* Workspace boundaries, reassignment and revoked access are enforced on delivery and opening.
* Existing missed-call, voicemail and email reply journeys are integrated and verified before claiming full CRM notification parity.
* Deferred expansion remains visible and is either delivered through reviewed follow-on scope or explicitly moved out of this master before closure.

## Name 23 and proof

Ship Alert the responsible rep when a client texts back independently to a controlled LT pilot once a test closer, eligible receiving line and authorized fallback are confirmed. Use consented test contacts. Preserve rollback of alert dispatch without stopping inbound message persistence. Do not backfill old inbox history as new alerts.

Proposed targets: persisted text to in-app attention p95 within five seconds under pilot load; ready incoming call event to card p95 within one second. Record provider delay separately. No unauthorized recipients or duplicate visible alerts in replay and multi-tab tests. These are acceptance targets, not measured current performance.

Browser permission being allowed is not proof that an operating-system banner appeared. Verify the actual banner, click destination, audio and denied/revoked states. Product activation instrumentation must use the repository's standard workflow and be verified in PostHog.

### Shared flag and pilot contract

Notifications v2 requires explicit workspace opt-in. The first cohort contains only test users whose current workspaces are all opted in; people with mixed memberships keep the complete existing feed. Membership/flag changes and queued delivery re-check eligibility. Elevated roles and partner grants do not implicitly enable the rollout. Source processing continues when notification delivery is disabled, and migration/rollback preserve existing notices and personal state. Before switching, old unfinished notices must be safely carried over with their original time/state and no new interruption; an unresolved mapping keeps that user on the existing feed and blocks final removal.

### Preview checks on demand

An authorized tester on an isolated preview can prepare fixtures, trigger any implemented notification source or run all enabled scenarios, replay an occurrence, advance scenario time, inspect results and reset only that run. Triggers use the real source handlers, persistence, jobs, recipient checks and delivery policy; they do not insert demonstration cards. External effects are captured at their provider boundary. Production cannot expose the runner.

ENG-13772 owns the minimal runner, fixtures and manifest; ENG-13774 supplies its small operator view; each producer owns its scenarios. ENG-13771 and ENG-13431 remain independent Wave 1 deliveries. Missing producer cases stay Pending until whichever producer or runner lands later completes integration. The report distinguishes source/preview checks from real OS/provider proof and lists parked/external cases honestly. The master’s shared AI context defines the full contract.

### Safe final cutover

The compatibility bridge and existing billing producers establish native warning parity before ENG-13777 removes Name 22. Full source/channel parity and a 100% rollout stable for one week precede the removal merge; a narrow pilot does not satisfy that gate. Billing remains independently deliverable. One PR per delivery remains the target, with an actual additions-plus-deletions size check before implementation. ENG-13772 coordinates its eight approved nested deliveries without an implementation PR of its own. No additional tickets or size exceptions are implicitly approved.

## Close guidance

* Close Inbox: use an actionable queue with separate read, Done and Future states, plus direct conversation actions.
* Close calling and SMS/MMS: guide the call, text and follow-up experience.
* Browser notification troubleshooting: distinguish an open ready app, site permission and OS notification settings. Our closed-tab push and advanced preference requirements go beyond the behavior confirmed in this research.

## Implementation context

AI context.md: shared end goal, rollout, QA and child-run contract. Read this context before planning or implementing any child. Revision: `ENG-13430/2026-09-14-r2`.

relatedSnapshot.title: Pop-ups, incoming calls, desktop notifications and sounds
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When something happens, a card slides in at the top right. Calls ring in their own slot above it. If the rep is in another tab they get a desktop notification, a sound and a count in the tab title, and a "While you were away" card when they come back.

## Problem

Today only calls pop up, and only on some routes. Texts, escalations and payment problems are silent until someone opens the drawer. There is no shared permission prompt or sound handling, so each feature would build its own.

## What's included

* `NotificationProvider` mounted once in `app/(saas)/providers.tsx`: one realtime connection per tab, React Query cache patched from stream events.
* Pop-up host: a second Sonner `Toaster` (id `notifications`), top right, 372px cards, 3 visible, fans out on hover. Bursts collapse ("Name 24 · 3 new messages"). Undo toasts stay at the bottom.
* Suppression: no pop-up while the drawer is open (the drawer card highlights instead) or when the related conversation is the visible route.
* Call slot: the incoming call card moves above the stack, restyled per design (frame fill, 16px radius, 372px, company, stage, number and line; Enter answers, Name 21 declines).
* Tab leader (Web Locks, `BroadcastChannel` fallback): one tab plays sound and shows desktop notifications.
* Name 25 notifications only when the tab is hidden, `tag` per group, `requireInteraction` for calls. Soft permission prompt "Hear about calls and replies while you're in another tab", shown only from a click, never on load. Blocked-permission recovery copy.
* `useNotificationSound`: unlocks on a user gesture. The "Sound is off · click to enable" chip appears in the pop-up slot only when a sound was actually suppressed. Sounds: ringtone, message, escalation, positive reply.
* Tab title "(n) Page · Acquisity" plus a favicon dot on the Acquisity logo.
* "While you were away" summary card on return.
* Design tokens: this ticket adds `ds-pill-bg`, `ds-border-strong`, `ds-red-solid` and `ds-shadow-pop` (light and dark values are in the prototype CSS) in one PR. The drawer and top bar alert tickets reuse them. If the drawer ticket starts first, it adds them instead.

## Incoming calls (merged from the old call reliability ticket)

* Keep the current Answer, Ignore and ring-mute controls working behind the new call card. Show workspace and called line.
* The call card and its alerts cover every signed-in page and supported workspace switches.
* Calling readiness distinguishes phone registration, microphone, sound and desktop notification permission, using live checks rather than remembered setup. A failed check says what the rep can fix and offers a retry or test.
* One tab owns ringing and the desktop alert; answer, ignore, caller hang-up, timeout, logout and closing the owner tab all clean up every tab.
* Clicking a current desktop alert focuses the answerable call. A stale alert never answers an ended call.
* Missed-call notifications are in ENG-13780. Call routing, ring groups, closed-app answering and native mobile calling are out of scope. Don't reopen canceled ENG-12501.

## Motion (from the prototype CSS, until the spec board lands)

* Pop-up in: `popIn .42s cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.25,1.05)`, from `translateX(110%)` and opacity 0.
* Stack fan: `fan .22s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)`, from `translateY(-8px)` and opacity .3.
* Name 25 banner (simulated in the prototype): `osIn .45s cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.25,1.05)`.
* Call ring pulse: `ring 1.4s ease-out infinite`, scale .92 to 1.35.
* All animation off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Design

Current design (5 Oct 2026): Notifications kit, clickable. Open the pop-up stack and hover it to fan the cards; the other links below go straight to calls, away states and the calling checks in Settings. The kit prototype is the source of truth for sizes, colours and motion; the screenshots are for orientation.

The prototype is private until James shares it; the screenshots here are the same frames.

* Pop-up stack (hover to fan)
* Text burst
* Incoming call (Enter answers, Name 21 declines)
* Away: desktop banners and tab count
* Away: caller hung up
* Settings, microphone blocked
* Settings, phone line offline
* Settings › Notifications

**Pop-up stack under the bell, dark**

**Text burst collapsed into one card**

**Incoming call ringing, light**

**Soft desktop permission prompt**

**In scope:** pop-up card, burst, collapsed and fanned stack, incoming call ringing and connected, desktop banner and tab count (the browser window frame in the screenshots is simulated), "While you were away", soft permission prompt, sound chip, the "Calling in this browser" checks, and dark mode for all of these.

**Not in scope:** the drawer, workspace alerts in the top bar and the rest of the settings page (their own tickets).

**Changed from the earlier design:**

* Pop-ups arrive under the bell, top right.
* The call card names the workspace and the line.
* A "Calling in this browser" section in Settings › Notifications shows phone line, microphone, ringtone and desktop permission, each with its fix (Reconnect, Check again, Test ringtone). This ticket owns it; it lives on the ENG-13776 page.
* A ringing desktop banner turns into "Missed call … They hung up after 24 seconds" when the caller hangs up. No stale Answer button.
* The tab title count and the favicon red dot are drawn.
* New sounds in a warm mallet voice, short and never a buzzer: the ringtone rises three notes, twice; a text is a soft two-note lift; an escalation is a brighter repeated pair; a positive reply is a quick arpeggio to a bell.

**Not drawn, build from the text above:** real OS banners (simulated in the frame) and the licensed sound files. Production uses licensed files with the same character as the kit sounds.

Superseded, do not build from: the 13 Sep prototype (link) and the design packs attached before 5 Oct.

## Build order

This ticket owns shared pop-ups, permission prompts, desktop notifications, sound and incoming-call presentation. ENG-13431 ships text and confirmed-failure notifications independently through today’s drawer, then consumes these shared surfaces when ready. The master’s current order settles the former overlap.

## Blocked by

ENG-13772

## Done when

* One event in two tabs gives one sound and one desktop banner.
* The visible conversation and an open drawer suppress pop-ups.
* Denied, revoked and re-granted permission states work.
* A real macOS banner, its click destination and the sound are verified in QA on Chrome and Safari.
* Both themes at 1280, 1440 and 1920; reduced motion honoured.
* An incoming call shows on foreground, background, minimized and non-sidebar pages for the authorized rep; two tabs give one audible alert; answering or the caller hanging up clears all ringing state.
* Revoked microphone or notification permission and phone registration failure show up without relying on old setup.
* Wrong-workspace users see no caller preview.
* PostHog `popup.shown`, `popup.clicked`, `desktop_permission.*` and `sound.unlocked` verified landing.

Size: about 2,000 lines.

## Shared roadmap and verification

Add this ticket’s real-source preview scenarios and verify the master’s flag, access, replay and evidence contract. Existing Wave 1 producers may ship before the runner; whichever side lands later completes integration and records the pending preview proof.

## Implementation context

AI context.md contains this ticket’s source seams, scope boundaries and QA handoff. Read the master plan and shared master AI context first. Shared revision: `ENG-13430/2026-09-14-r2`. Use the existing 15-ticket structure and native blockers; do not create or revive tickets automatically.
